channel.description: What officeholders said each day from or about New York, and which statements government data supports, contradicts or rules out.

item.title: Said & Checked, New York, 2026-11-18: none false or contradicted, 3 unsettled (Chuck Schumer)
item.description:
No statement was found false or contradicted.

Unsettled

  • Chuck Schumer, U.S. Senator from New York: “and I have the votes to continue serving as Democratic Leader” Unsettled. The Dec. 1 Senate Democratic leadership vote is a secret ballot that has not yet been held, and no public count shows a majority of the caucus backing Schumer. Published tallies of declared support (reported as about 14 for Schumer, 4 for Van Hollen and 38 uncommitted) decide nothing either way.
  • Chuck Schumer, U.S. Senator from New York: “Trump arrived in Manila only 30 minutes before the summit ended and is off to China tomorrow to spend the rest of the week with Xi Jinping.” Unsettled. Pre-trip reports from AFP and from ANI (citing the White House) said Trump was due in Manila on the evening of Nov. 17, 'near the summit's conclusion', with a Nov. 18 Marcos visit and then Shenzhen, so the departure for China matches. No report found gives his actual landing time or when the summit closed, so '30 minutes' was neither confirmed nor ruled out.
  • Chuck Schumer, U.S. Senator from New York: “Forget explaining why his administration didn't reveal that a Chinese spy infiltrated one of America's leading companies.” Unsettled. The espionage claim rests on a New York Times report, carried by AP, that U.S. officials concluded the woman involved was a Chinese spy. Nvidia's board says it has no reason to believe secrets were compromised, Singapore authorities found insufficient evidence of a crime, and the FBI and board inquiries are open. No official finding of infiltration or of administration non-disclosure was found.
